tweets.text: Back to steering wheel and pedals

No steering wheel. No pedals. No Driver. 

Just tap Start Ride.  

This is a full Tesla Cybercab drive in Austin — Tesla’s purpose-built two-seater robotaxi with no manual controls. No walkaround.   
Just the ride.  

Once both people are in, the butterfly doors close, you hit Start Ride on the 21-inch screen, and the car takes over.   

Early rides keep landing on the same thing: quiet, soft, and almost boring.  

It pulls away smoothly, handles speed bumps without drama, and mostly disappears into the background. Which is exactly what you want from a driverless taxi.  The cabin feels more like a lounge than a car. 

The bench slides and reclines, the legroom is bigger than the body looks, and the whole trip runs off that center screen plus climate and seat controls.   

Starlink is built in for video, games, and entertainment while the car handles the road.

Cybercab is Tesla’s first vehicle designed only for unsupervised autonomy.   

Model Y robotaxis already carried paying riders. This is the car built around that software. @elonmusk @tesla @robotaxi @Tesla_AI @EricETesla @aelluswamy
